policy_name: Crestview Mutual Health CG-RAD-12: MRI of the Lumbar Spine (illustrative)

criteria.criterion: Indication A - At least 6 weeks of documented conservative therapy with persistent symptoms
criteria.evidence: Symptoms began about {{ONSET}}; conservative care (NSAIDs, oral steroids, 6 PT visits) is documented from {{VISIT1}}, about 4.3 weeks before the MRI on {{DOS}}.

citation.excerpt: About 5 weeks since symptom onset; completed oral steroids, on naproxen, 6 PT visits.

criteria.action_needed: Do not rely on Indication A; argue Indication B1.

criteria.criterion: Indication B1 - Progressive or severe neurological deficit, documented by comparing serial examinations
criteria.evidence: Initial exam {{VISIT1}}: strength 5/5 including left EHL and dorsiflexion. Follow-up {{VISIT2}}: left EHL 4/5 and dorsiflexion 4+/5, documented by the physician as a new motor deficit progressing despite conservative care.
criteria.action_needed: Quote both exams side by side in the appeal.

criteria.evidence: PT progress note on {{PT_LAST}} records new difficulty heel-walking on the left and refers the patient back to the physician.

citation.excerpt: Notes new difficulty with heel walking on the left at today's visit.

criteria.criterion: Indication C - Pre-procedural planning once a procedure is actively considered
criteria.evidence: The MRI order states it will 'guide possible epidural steroid injection or surgical referral', but no injection or surgical plan is documented afterward in the uploaded records.

citation.excerpt: MRI... to evaluate for a compressive lesion and guide possible epidural steroid injection or surgical referral.

criteria.action_needed: If an ESI or surgical consult followed the MRI, attach that note to strengthen Indication C.

criteria.criterion: No red flags for cauda equina, infection, malignancy or fracture (B2/B3)
criteria.evidence: The notes explicitly document no bowel/bladder change, no saddle anesthesia, no fever, weight loss or cancer history. B2/B3 do not apply.

citation.excerpt: No bowel/bladder changes, no saddle anesthesia, no fever, no weight loss, no history of cancer.

overall_assessment: The case turns on Indication B1. Serial exams document a new motor deficit, which the policy explicitly lists as a red flag, and the MRI confirmed a concordant compressive lesion. The deficit is mild and was seen on one follow-up, so the outcome depends on the reviewer accepting it as 'progressive'.
documents_to_attach: New patient visit note ({{VISIT1}}) - baseline 5/5 strength
Follow-up visit note ({{VISIT2}}) - new 4/5 EHL weakness
Any post-MRI ESI or surgical referral note
gaps: Conservative care is under 6 weeks, so Indication A cannot be used.
No post-MRI treatment plan is documented in the uploaded record.
